subject: maths
title: Primary 5 Area of Triangles: Base, Height and Composite Figures
seo_title: P5 Area of Triangle Worksheets: Free Primary 5 Maths Practice with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Concepts of base and height of a triangle; area of triangle; area of composite figures made up of rectangles, squares and triangles
meta_desc: Free P5 area of triangle practice: base and height, ½ × base × height, missing heights, composite figures and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Area of triangle = ½ × base × height.
key_sub: The height is perpendicular to the base, not a slanted side: base 14 m, height 12 m gives ½ × 14 × 12 = 84 m².
body_html:
Base and height

Any side of a triangle can be the base. The height is the line from the opposite vertex that is perpendicular to the base. It is drawn as a dashed line with a small square at the right angle.

In an obtuse-angled triangle, the height can fall outside the triangle. Extend the base with a dashed line and draw the height to it.

In a right-angled triangle, the two sides that meet at the right angle are a base and its height.

Area of a triangle

A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height. So

Area of triangle = 12 × base × height

Find a missing height

A triangle has an area of 36 cm² and a base of 9 cm. Find its height.

12 × 9 × ? = 36. Double the area: 36 × 2 = 72. Then 72 ÷ 9 = 8.

Answer: 8 cm

Composite figures

Divide the figure into rectangles, squares and triangles. Find each area, then add. Or find the area of the whole rectangle and subtract the part that is not shaded.

Shaded triangle in a rectangle

A rectangle is 14 cm by 8 cm. A shaded triangle has the 14 cm side as its base and its top vertex on the opposite side. Find the shaded area.

The height of the triangle is the breadth of the rectangle, 8 cm. 12 × 14 × 8 = 56.

Answer: 56 cm², half of the rectangle

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the slanted 13 m side as the heightUse the height that is perpendicular to the base: 12 m
Area = 14 × 12 = 168 m²Do not forget the 12: 12 × 14 × 12 = 84 m²
Height = 36 ÷ 9 = 4 cmDouble the area first: 36 × 2 ÷ 9 = 8 cm
Writing 84 m for an areaArea is in square units: 84 m²
Thinking the height must be inside the triangleIn an obtuse-angled triangle it can be outside

faq.q: What is taught in P5 area of triangle?
faq.a: Primary 5 students learn to identify the base and height of a triangle, find its area with 1/2 × base × height, and find the area of composite figures made up of rectangles, squares and triangles.

faq.q: How do I explain the height of a triangle to my child?
faq.a: The height is the line from a vertex that meets the opposite side (the base) at a right angle. It is not a slanted side, and in an obtuse-angled triangle it can fall outside the triangle.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with area of triangles?
faq.a: Forgetting the 1/2, or using the slanted side as the height. A triangle with base 14 m and height 12 m has an area of 1/2 × 14 × 12 = 84 m², not 168 m².

faq.q: Is area of triangle in the MOE syllabus for Primary 5?
faq.a: Yes. Area of triangle and composite figures is in Area and Volume, Measurement and Geometry, for Primary 5 in the MOE 2021 syllabus. It is used again in Primary 6 and in PSLE questions.

sets.title: Base and height of a triangle

items.q: LM is the base of triangle KLM. Which line is the height?
items.e: KN is the height. It is outside the triangle because the triangle has an obtuse angle. It meets the base line LM (extended with the grey dashed line) at a right angle. KL and KM are slanted sides.

items.q: Triangle ABC has two dashed heights. Which line is the height for the base AC?
items.e: BE meets AC at a right angle. AD is the height for the base BC. Every side can be a base, and each base has its own height.

items.q: QR is the base of triangle PQR. Which line is the height?
items.e: PS is perpendicular to the base QR: it meets QR at a right angle (see the small square). PQ and PR are slanted sides, not the height.

items.q: Triangle ABC has a right angle at B. AB is the base. Which line is the height?
items.e: BC meets AB at a right angle at B, so BC is the height. In a right-angled triangle, the two sides that meet at the right angle are a base and its height.

items.q: Triangle ABC has a right angle at B. AC is the base. Which line is the height?
items.e: BD meets AC at a right angle at D, so BD is the height. In a right-angled triangle, the two sides that meet at the right angle are a base and its height.

items.q: FG is the base of triangle EFG. Which line is the height?
items.e: EH is perpendicular to the base FG: it meets FG at a right angle (see the small square). EF and EG are slanted sides, not the height.

items.q: How many different sides of a triangle can be used as its base?
items.e: Any of the 3 sides can be the base. Each base has its own height, drawn from the opposite vertex.

items.q: The base of this right-angled triangle is 12 cm. What is its height?
items.e: The 5 cm side meets the 12 cm base at a right angle, so the height is 5 cm. The 13 cm side is slanted.

items.q: Triangle ABC has two dashed heights. Which line is the height for the base BC?
items.e: AD meets BC at a right angle. BE is the height for the base AC. Every side can be a base, and each base has its own height.

items.q: KL is the base of triangle JKL. Which line is the height?
items.e: JM is perpendicular to the base KL: it meets KL at a right angle (see the small square). JK and JL are slanted sides, not the height.

items.q: The base of the triangle is 28 cm. What is its height?
items.e: The height is the dashed line, perpendicular to the base: 24 cm. The 26 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: The base of the triangle is 21 cm. What is its height?
items.e: The height is the dashed line, perpendicular to the base: 8 cm. The 17 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: The base of the triangle is 11 m. What is its height?
items.e: The height is the dashed line, perpendicular to the base: 12 m. The 20 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: Which sentence about the height of a triangle is always true?
c: It is perpendicular to the base.
It is one of the sides.
items.e: The height is always perpendicular to the base. It is not always a side, and in an obtuse-angled triangle it can be outside the triangle.

items.q: Triangle ABC has a right angle at B. BC is the base. Which line is the height?
items.e: AB meets BC at a right angle at B, so AB is the height. In a right-angled triangle, the two sides that meet at the right angle are a base and its height.

items.q: BC is the base of triangle ABC. Which line is the height?
items.e: AE is the height. It is outside the triangle because the triangle has an obtuse angle. It meets the base line BC (extended with the grey dashed line) at a right angle. AB and AC are slanted sides.

items.q: YZ is the base of triangle XYZ. Which line is the height?
items.e: XW is the height. It is outside the triangle because the triangle has an obtuse angle. It meets the base line YZ (extended with the grey dashed line) at a right angle. XY and XZ are slanted sides.

items.q: ST is the base of triangle RST. Which line is the height?
items.e: RU is perpendicular to the base ST: it meets ST at a right angle (see the small square). RS and RT are slanted sides, not the height.

items.q: QR is the base of triangle PQR. Which line is the height?
items.e: PT is perpendicular to the base QR: it meets QR at a right angle (see the small square). PQ and PR are slanted sides, not the height.

items.q: BC is the base of triangle ABC. Which line is the height?
items.e: AD is the height. It is outside the triangle because the triangle has an obtuse angle. It meets the base line BC (extended with the grey dashed line) at a right angle. AB and AC are slanted sides.

sets.title: Area of a triangle: ½ × base × height

items.q: A triangle has a base of 16 cm and a height of 9 cm. Find its area.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 16 × 9 = 72 cm². Do not forget the 12.

items.q: Find the area of the right-angled triangle.
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. Area = 12 × 24 × 10 = 120 cm². The 26 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: Which gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 12 cm and the height is the dashed 15 cm line, which meets the base line at a right angle outside the triangle. Area = 12 × 12 × 15 = 90 cm².

items.q: Find the area of the triangle.
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it is perpendicular to the base. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 7 × 12 = 42 m². The 20 m side is slanted, so it is not the height. The triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height is outside it.

items.q: Find the area of the triangle.
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it is perpendicular to the base. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 25 × 24 = 300 m². The 40 m side is slanted, so it is not the height. The triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height is outside it.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 24 cm and a height of 11 cm. Find its area.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 24 × 11 = 132 cm². Do not forget the 12.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 15 m and a height of 7 m. Find its area.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 15 × 7 = 52.5 m². Do not forget the 12.

items.q: Find the area of the triangle.
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it is perpendicular to the base. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 24 × 16 = 192 cm². The 20 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: Find the area of the triangle.
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it is perpendicular to the base. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 21 × 10 = 105 cm². The 14.5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A diagonal cuts the rectangle into two equal triangles. Find the area of the shaded triangle.
items.e: The rectangle is 9 × 4 = 36 m². The shaded triangle is half of it: 12 × 9 × 4 = 18 m².

items.q: Find the area of the right-angled triangle.
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. Area = 12 × 18 × 24 = 216 cm². The 30 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: Find the area of the right-angled triangle.
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. Area = 12 × 6 × 8 = 24 m². The 10 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A diagonal cuts the rectangle into two equal triangles. Find the area of the shaded triangle.
items.e: The rectangle is 13 × 6 = 78 cm². The shaded triangle is half of it: 12 × 13 × 6 = 39 cm².

items.q: Find the area of the right-angled triangle.
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. Area = 12 × 8 × 15 = 60 m². The 17 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: Find the area of the triangle.
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it is perpendicular to the base. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 18 × 12 = 108 cm². The 15 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: Find the area of the triangle.
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it is perpendicular to the base. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 14 × 24 = 168 m². The 40 m side is slanted, so it is not the height. The triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height is outside it.

items.q: Find the area of the triangle.
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it is perpendicular to the base. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 19 × 12 = 114 m². The 37 m side is slanted, so it is not the height. The triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height is outside it.

items.q: Which gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 15 m and the height is the dashed 6 m line, which meets the base line at a right angle outside the triangle. Area = 12 × 15 × 6 = 45 m².

items.q: Find the area of the triangle.
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it is perpendicular to the base. Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 14 × 12 = 84 cm². The 15 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 4.5 m and a height of 6 m. Find its area.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height = 12 × 4.5 × 6 = 13.5 m². Do not forget the 12.

sets.title: Find the missing base or height

items.q: A triangle has an area of 120 cm² and a base of 15 cm. What is its height?
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 15 × ? = 120. Double the area: 120 × 2 = 240. Then 240 ÷ 15 = 16 cm. Check: 12 × 15 × 16 = 120 cm².

items.q: The area of a triangle is 70 m². Its height is 10 m. How long is its base?
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 10 × ? = 70. Double the area: 70 × 2 = 140. Then 140 ÷ 10 = 14 m. Check: 12 × 10 × 14 = 70 m².

items.q: The area of a triangle is 85 m². Its height is 10 m. How long is its base?
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 10 × ? = 85. Double the area: 85 × 2 = 170. Then 170 ÷ 10 = 17 m. Check: 12 × 10 × 17 = 85 m².

items.q: A right-angled triangle has an area of 30 cm². One of the two sides that meet at the right angle is 5 cm. How long is the other one?
items.e: The two sides at the right angle are the base and the height. 30 × 2 = 60, and 60 ÷ 5 = 12 cm. Check: 12 × 5 × 12 = 30 cm².

items.q: The area of the triangle is 240 cm². Find its height.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 20 × ? = 240. Double the area: 240 × 2 = 480. Then 480 ÷ 20 = 24 cm. Check: 12 × 20 × 24 = 240 cm².

items.q: A triangle has an area of 96 cm² and a base of 16 cm. What is its height?
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 16 × ? = 96. Double the area: 96 × 2 = 192. Then 192 ÷ 16 = 12 cm. Check: 12 × 16 × 12 = 96 cm².

items.q: A right-angled triangle has an area of 54 m². One of the two sides that meet at the right angle is 9 m. How long is the other one?
items.e: The two sides at the right angle are the base and the height. 54 × 2 = 108, and 108 ÷ 9 = 12 m. Check: 12 × 9 × 12 = 54 m².

items.q: The area of the triangle is 24 m². Find its base.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 12 × ? = 24. Double the area: 24 × 2 = 48. Then 48 ÷ 12 = 4 m. Check: 12 × 12 × 4 = 24 m².

items.q: The area of the triangle is 90 cm². Find its height.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 18 × ? = 90. Double the area: 90 × 2 = 180. Then 180 ÷ 18 = 10 cm. Check: 12 × 18 × 10 = 90 cm².

items.q: The area of the triangle is 12 m². Find its base.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 4 × ? = 12. Double the area: 12 × 2 = 24. Then 24 ÷ 4 = 6 m. Check: 12 × 4 × 6 = 12 m².

items.q: The area of the triangle is 27 m². Find its height.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 9 × ? = 27. Double the area: 27 × 2 = 54. Then 54 ÷ 9 = 6 m. Check: 12 × 9 × 6 = 27 m².

items.q: The area of the triangle is 132 m². Find its height.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 11 × ? = 132. Double the area: 132 × 2 = 264. Then 264 ÷ 11 = 24 m. Check: 12 × 11 × 24 = 132 m².

items.q: The area of the triangle is 66 cm². Find its height.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 11 × ? = 66. Double the area: 66 × 2 = 132. Then 132 ÷ 11 = 12 cm. Check: 12 × 11 × 12 = 66 cm².

items.q: The area of the triangle is 21 cm². Find its base.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 6 × ? = 21. Double the area: 21 × 2 = 42. Then 42 ÷ 6 = 7 cm. Check: 12 × 6 × 7 = 21 cm².

items.q: A triangle has an area of 40 cm² and a base of 20 cm. What is its height?
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 20 × ? = 40. Double the area: 40 × 2 = 80. Then 80 ÷ 20 = 4 cm. Check: 12 × 20 × 4 = 40 cm².

items.q: The area of a triangle is 56 m². Its height is 16 m. How long is its base?
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 16 × ? = 56. Double the area: 56 × 2 = 112. Then 112 ÷ 16 = 7 m. Check: 12 × 16 × 7 = 56 m².

items.q: Triangle P has a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm. Triangle Q has the same area and a base of 4 cm. What is the height of triangle Q?
items.e: Area of P = 12 × 10 × 6 = 30 cm². For Q: 30 × 2 = 60, and 60 ÷ 4 = 15 cm. Check: 12 × 4 × 15 = 30 cm².

items.q: A triangle has an area of 35 cm² and a base of 7 cm. What is its height?
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 7 × ? = 35. Double the area: 35 × 2 = 70. Then 70 ÷ 7 = 10 cm. Check: 12 × 7 × 10 = 35 cm².

items.q: The area of the triangle is 243 m². Find its height.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 27 × ? = 243. Double the area: 243 × 2 = 486. Then 486 ÷ 27 = 18 m. Check: 12 × 27 × 18 = 243 m².

items.q: The area of the triangle is 12 cm². Find its base.
items.e: Area = 12 × base × height, so 12 × 3 × ? = 12. Double the area: 12 × 2 = 24. Then 24 ÷ 3 = 8 cm. Check: 12 × 3 × 8 = 12 cm².

items.q: The figure is made up of a rectangle and a triangle. Find its area.
items.e: The triangle’s height is 11 − 4 = 7 cm. Rectangle: 16 × 4 = 64 cm². Triangle: 12 × 16 × 7 = 56 cm². Total: 64 + 56 = 120 cm².

items.q: A right-angled triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). Find the area of the figure that is left.
items.e: Whole rectangle: 8 × 9 = 72 m². Triangle cut off: 12 × 3 × 4 = 6 m². Area left: 72 − 6 = 66 m².

items.q: The dashed line divides the figure into a rectangle and a triangle. Find its area.
items.e: Rectangle: 5 × 7 = 35 cm². The triangle’s base is 9 − 5 = 4 cm and its height is 7 cm: 12 × 4 × 7 = 14 cm². Total: 35 + 14 = 49 cm².

items.q: The figure is made up of a rectangle and two identical triangles. Find its area.
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 8 = 48 cm². Each triangle: base 8 cm, height 5 cm, so 12 × 8 × 5 = 20 cm². Total: 48 + 20 + 20 = 88 cm².

items.q: The figure is made up of a rectangle and a triangle. Find its area.
items.e: Rectangle: 16 × 8 = 128 cm². Triangle: 12 × 16 × 7 = 56 cm². Total: 128 + 56 = 184 cm².

items.q: The figure is made up of a square and a triangle. Find its area.
items.e: Square: 12 × 12 = 144 m². Triangle: 12 × 12 × 4 = 24 m². Total: 144 + 24 = 168 m².

items.q: A right-angled triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). Find the area of the figure that is left.
items.e: Whole rectangle: 14 × 9 = 126 cm². Triangle cut off: 12 × 4 × 2 = 4 cm². Area left: 126 − 4 = 122 cm².

items.q: The top vertex of the shaded triangle is on the top side of the rectangle. Find its area.
items.e: Base: 10 cm. The height is the distance between the top and bottom sides, the breadth of the rectangle: 8 cm. Area = 12 × 10 × 8 = 40 cm². (The length 18 cm is not needed.)

items.q: Find the area of the shaded triangle in the square.
items.e: The triangle’s base is the 10 m side. Its top vertex is on the opposite side, so its height is 10 m, the breadth of the square. Area = 12 × 10 × 10 = 50 m². It is half of the square.

items.q: The figure is made up of a rectangle and a triangle. Find its area.
items.e: Rectangle: 11 × 6 = 66 cm². The triangle’s base is the 6 cm side and its height is 7 cm: 12 × 6 × 7 = 21 cm². Total: 66 + 21 = 87 cm².

items.q: The top vertex of the shaded triangle is on the top side of the rectangle. Find its area.
items.e: Base: 9 m. The height is the distance between the top and bottom sides, the breadth of the rectangle: 6 m. Area = 12 × 9 × 6 = 27 m². (The length 15 m is not needed.)

items.q: The figure is made up of a rectangle and a triangle. Find its area.
items.e: The triangle’s height is 11 − 5 = 6 m. Rectangle: 10 × 5 = 50 m². Triangle: 12 × 10 × 6 = 30 m². Total: 50 + 30 = 80 m².

items.q: A right-angled triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). Find the area of the figure that is left.
items.e: Whole rectangle: 13 × 10 = 130 m². Triangle cut off: 12 × 6 × 4 = 12 m². Area left: 130 − 12 = 118 m².

items.q: The figure is made up of a rectangle and two identical triangles. Find its area.
items.e: Rectangle: 11 × 10 = 110 m². Each triangle: base 10 m, height 5 m, so 12 × 10 × 5 = 25 m². Total: 110 + 25 + 25 = 160 m².

items.q: Find the area of the shaded triangle in the rectangle.
items.e: The triangle’s base is the 14 cm side. Its top vertex is on the opposite side, so its height is 8 cm, the breadth of the rectangle. Area = 12 × 14 × 8 = 56 cm². It is half of the rectangle.

items.q: The top vertex of the shaded triangle is on the top side of the rectangle. Find its area.
items.e: Base: 7 cm. The height is the distance between the top and bottom sides, the breadth of the rectangle: 12 cm. Area = 12 × 7 × 12 = 42 cm². (The length 20 cm is not needed.)

items.q: The figure is made up of a rectangle and a triangle. Find its area.
items.e: Rectangle: 13 × 6 = 78 m². The triangle’s base is the 6 m side and its height is 5 m: 12 × 6 × 5 = 15 m². Total: 78 + 15 = 93 m².

items.q: Find the total area of the two shaded triangles.
items.e: Rectangle: 16 × 9 = 144 cm². The white triangle: 12 × 16 × 9 = 72 cm². Shaded: 144 − 72 = 72 cm². The shaded parts are always half of the rectangle.

items.q: The figure is made up of a rectangle and a triangle. Find its area.
items.e: Rectangle: 7 × 6 = 42 cm². The triangle’s base is the 6 cm side and its height is 4 cm: 12 × 6 × 4 = 12 cm². Total: 42 + 12 = 54 cm².

items.q: The dashed line divides the figure into a rectangle and a triangle. Find its area.
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 4 = 24 m². The triangle’s base is 13 − 6 = 7 m and its height is 4 m: 12 × 7 × 4 = 14 m². Total: 24 + 14 = 38 m².

sets.title: Word problems: flags, gardens and bar models

items.q: A triangular section of a wall at a playground has a base of 6 m and a height of 4 m. One litre of paint covers 3 m². How many litres of paint are needed for the section?
items.e: Area = 12 × 6 × 4 = 12 m². Paint: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 ℓ. (8 ℓ forgets the 12; 36 ℓ multiplies instead of dividing.)

items.q: The area of a rectangle is 4 times the area of a triangle. The rectangle’s area is 54 cm² more than the triangle’s. What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The difference is 4 − 1 = 3 units. 3 units = 54 cm², so 1 unit = 54 ÷ 3 = 18 cm². (13.5 cm² divides by 4 instead of 3.)

items.q: A garden patch at the void deck of an HDB block is a right-angled triangle. The two sides along the walls are 6 m and 8 m, and the third side is 10 m. Grass costs $5 for each square metre. How much does the grass cost?
items.e: The 6 m and 8 m sides meet at a right angle. Area = 12 × 6 × 8 = 24 m². Cost: 24 × $5 = $120. ($200 uses the slanted 10 m side.)

items.q: A Children’s Day poster is a square of side 60 cm. The shaded triangle has the bottom side as its base and its top vertex on the top side. What is the area of the shaded triangle?
items.e: The height of the triangle is the side of the square, 60 cm. Area = 12 × 60 × 60 = 1800 cm², half of the square.

items.q: Two triangles share the same base of 14 cm. One has a height of 9 cm and the other has a height of 5 cm. How much greater is the area of the taller triangle?
items.e: Taller: 12 × 14 × 9 = 63 cm². Shorter: 12 × 14 × 5 = 35 cm². Difference: 63 − 35 = 28 cm².

items.q: Mei Ling has a rectangular card 30 cm long and 20 cm wide. She cuts out a triangle with a base of 18 cm on one long side and its top vertex on the opposite side. What is the area of the card left?
items.e: Card: 30 × 20 = 600 cm². The triangle’s height is the width of the card, 20 cm: 12 × 18 × 20 = 180 cm². Left: 600 − 180 = 420 cm².

items.q: Hui Min’s triangular vegetable plot has an area of 45 m². Its height is 6 m. What is the length of its base?
items.e: 12 × ? × 6 = 45. Double the area: 45 × 2 = 90. 90 ÷ 6 = 15 m. (7.5 m forgets to double.)

items.q: For National Day, Siti’s class makes 15 triangular flags. Each flag has a base of 20 cm and a height of 30 cm. What is the total area of the flags?
items.e: One flag: 12 × 20 × 30 = 300 cm². 15 flags: 15 × 300 = 4500 cm². (9000 cm² forgets the 12.)

items.q: A triangular plot of grass at East Coast Park has a base of 40 m and a height of 25 m. Its slanted sides are 30 m and 32 m long. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 12 × 40 × 25 = 500 m². The 30 m and 32 m sides are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: Raju draws a square of side 12 cm. He joins two corners at the bottom to the midpoint of the top side to make a triangle. What fraction of the square is the triangle?
items.e: Square: 12 × 12 = 144 cm². Triangle: base 12 cm, height 12 cm, so 12 × 12 × 12 = 72 cm². 72 out of 144 is 12.

items.q: Kumar draws a rectangle 16 cm by 10 cm and a white triangle inside it. The two triangles at the sides are shaded. What is the total shaded area?
items.e: Rectangle: 16 × 10 = 160 cm². White triangle: 12 × 16 × 10 = 80 cm². Shaded: 160 − 80 = 80 cm².

items.q: The area of triangle P is 3 times the area of triangle Q. Their total area is 96 cm². What is the area of triangle P?
items.e: 4 units = 96 cm². 1 unit = 96 ÷ 4 = 24 cm². Triangle P = 3 units = 3 × 24 = 72 cm².

items.q: Mr Tan’s rectangular garden is 12 m long and 9 m wide. It has a triangular flower bed with a base of 6 m and a height of 4 m. The rest is grass. What is the area of the grass?
items.e: Garden: 12 × 9 = 108 m². Flower bed: 12 × 6 × 4 = 12 m². Grass: 108 − 12 = 96 m². (84 m² forgets the 12.)

items.q: Wei Ming makes a kite from two triangles. They share a 40 cm stick as their base. Their heights are 15 cm and 35 cm. What is the area of the kite?
items.e: Top triangle: 12 × 40 × 15 = 300 cm². Bottom triangle: 12 × 40 × 35 = 700 cm². Kite: 300 + 700 = 1000 cm².

items.q: A signboard at a hawker centre is a rectangle 80 cm long and 30 cm wide with a triangle at one end, like an arrow. The triangle’s base is the 30 cm side and its height is 20 cm. What is the area of the signboard?
items.e: Rectangle: 80 × 30 = 2400 cm². Triangle: 12 × 30 × 20 = 300 cm². Total: 2400 + 300 = 2700 cm².

items.q: Xin Yi folds a square piece of paper of side 15 cm along a diagonal to make a triangle. What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The two sides of the square meet at a right angle, so they are the base and the height. Area = 12 × 15 × 15 = 112.5 cm², half of the square (225 cm²).

items.q: A triangular banner for Sports Day has a base of 1.2 m and a height of 80 cm. What is its area in square metres?
items.e: Use the same unit: 80 cm = 0.8 m. Area = 12 × 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.48 m². (48 m² mixes metres and centimetres.)

items.q: At a CCA camp, each end of a tent is a triangle with a base of 2 m and a height of 1.5 m. What is the total area of the two triangular ends?
items.e: One end: 12 × 2 × 1.5 = 1.5 m². Two ends: 2 × 1.5 = 3 m².

items.q: The area of triangle A is 18 cm² more than the area of triangle B. Their total area is 90 cm². What is the area of triangle A?
items.e: Take away the extra 18 cm²: 90 − 18 = 72 cm² = 2 units. 1 unit = 72 ÷ 2 = 36 cm² (triangle B). Triangle A = 36 + 18 = 54 cm².

items.q: The sail of Ahmad’s model boat is a triangle with an area of 150 cm². Its base is 15 cm. What is its height?
items.e: 12 × 15 × ? = 150. Double the area: 150 × 2 = 300. 300 ÷ 15 = 20 cm. Check: 12 × 15 × 20 = 150 cm².
